## Update: Custom Linux session stuck again

Same session (`ses_fac65f4ebffe8AZ7nFgr3oPkVs`), third time stuck.

### Pattern confirmed

1. Bash tool shows command as "running" after completion
2. Session stops responding to user messages
3. Deleting the stuck part from the database restores responsiveness

### Workaround

Run this to delete stuck parts:

```python
import sqlite3, json
session_id = "<stuck_session_id>"
db_path = "/home/dwc/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db"
conn = sqlite3.connect(db_path)
c = conn.cursor()
c.execute("SELECT id, data FROM part WHERE session_id = ?", (session_id,))
for pid, pdata in c.fetchall():
    pd = json.loads(pdata)
    if pd.get("type") == "tool" and pd.get("state", {}).get("status") == "running":
        c.execute("DELETE FROM part WHERE id = ?", (pid,))
conn.commit()
conn.close()
```

Then restart the opencode server.

### Note

This workaround only works if the session hasn't been corrupted by previous edits. If it returns "messages do not match ModelMessage[] schema", the session is permanently broken.

## Critical: Restarting opencode via bash tool requires full CPU reboot

### Problem

When the agent tries to restart the opencode web server using the bash tool:

```bash
pkill -f "opencode web --hostname 0.0.0.0" && sleep 2 && /home/dwc/.opencode/bin/opencode web --hostname 0.0.0.0 &
```

The command completes but opencode becomes unresponsive. A full CPU reboot is required to recover.

### Reproduction

1. Agent runs the restart command via bash tool
2. Command appears to complete
3. opencode stops responding to all sessions
4. Server restart does not fix it
5. Only a full CPU reboot recovers the system

### Affected sessions

- This has happened multiple times during this conversation
- Requires user to physically reboot their machine each time

### Impact

- User loses all active session state
- Productive work is interrupted
- User must manually restart their computer

### Suggestion

opencode should:
1. Never allow the agent to restart the server it is running on
2. Add a safety check that prevents killing the parent process
3. Document that server restarts must be done manually by the user
4. Consider a "server restart" button in the UI instead of bash commands

Thanks for the triage. Three points:

1. Not a strict duplicate of #37852 That report covers a stream ending mid-turn being recorded as a clean stop (finish=unknown, zero usage, no text, nothing logged). This report is the AbortError path: the fiber is interrupted, the turn is marked "interrupted" in the UI, and the error only shows up in the sidecar log. Different failure mode, but same underlying gap — transient stream failures are neither retried nor surfaced as recoverable errors. Happy to have this consolidated under #37852 (or a shared fix) if the maintainers prefer.

2. On @xylophoneengine's degraded-gateway hypothesis It would explain the trigger on my side too — my logs confirm I'm on the same opencode/opencode-go gateway (providerID=opencode-go, modelID=glm-5.3-flash for the main agent; the gpt-5.4-nano entries are only opencode's internal small model for auto-titling sessions). But the actionable bug on opencode's side stands regardless of gateway health: no automatic retry, and no visible error — just a silent "interrupted" turn.

3. Update on the retryability track (#48761 / PR #48710) #48761 was just fixed by PR #48710 (merged today, 2026-09-13), which bumps @ai-sdk/gateway to 3.0.191 so response-body network errors are now classified as retryable. My Desktop build (1.18.30) predates that bump, so this AbortError path may be covered by it. I'll retest on the next Desktop release — if random "interrupted" turns still reproduce after the bump, this report stands (the PR covers response-body network errors, not the Effect.onInterrupt fiber path specifically); if it's gone, feel free to close this as fixed by #48710.

I checked the `needs:issue` warning: this PR already references #48720 with `Closes #48720`. It targets `beta` for the V2 transport regression; the repository default is `dev`.

The [standards workflow](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/df23b7f9488a38e6f8064a0739d4f8cde86d7cfb/.github/workflows/pr-standards.yml) checks only `closingIssuesReferences`, which is empty here. [GitHub only interprets closing keywords for PRs targeting the default branch](https://docs.github.com/en/issues/tracking-your-work-with-issues/using-issues/linking-a-pull-request-to-an-issue#about-linked-issues-and-pull-requests), so this check treats the beta PR as missing an issue despite the existing reference.

Could a maintainer manually link #48720 in Development and clear the incorrect `needs:issue` label?

This issue might be a duplicate of an existing issue. Please check:
- #48805: Same exact error message — `reasoning `encrypted_content` was not issued to this caller` — occurring when switching models in the same session with the `muse-spark` family on the Console/Zen provider.

If your situation differs (e.g. you are not switching models mid-session), please add more context including your model, provider, and steps to reproduce so maintainers can distinguish it.

> * [bug: tool-result media 400s whole request for models without attachment capability #41163](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/41163): Same underlying path — tool-result media causing provider request failures due to `supportsMediaInToolResult` logic in `message-v2.ts`; your issue extends this specifically to PDF attachments on strict OpenAI-compatible gateways via the synthetic user message content array.
> * [Memory leak: PDF attachments are base64-encoded without size limit and re-encoded every turn, causing OOM #42263](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/42263): Overlapping root cause — PDF attachments from the `read` tool stored as base64 in history and re-sent on every turn (memory/OOM angle, but same data flow).
> * [Images in tool results bypass model modality check (text-only models receive base64 images) #39824](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/issues/39824): Related — media from tool results bypassing model modality checks.
> 
> If your issue is distinct enough (422 on user message content array specifically), feel free to clarify how it differs from the above.

Thanks for the triage! I checked the three referenced issues. Mine is related but has a distinct failure surface — happy to consolidate if maintainers prefer, but flagging what is unique here:

**vs. #41163** — same `supportsMediaInToolResult` path, but in my case the tool result itself was correctly degraded to a plain string (`"PDF read successfully"`). The failure happens one step later: the **synthetic user message** built at `message-v2.ts:380-399` produces a `content` **array** (`[text, file]`), and strict OpenAI-compatible gateways reject user-role content arrays entirely:

422 messages.297.user.content.str: Input should be a valid string

Note the model's declared modalities say PDF is supported (`glm-5.3-flash` → `input: ["text","image","video","pdf"]`), so `unsupportedParts()` never degrades the `file` block — and even if it did, the array would still not collapse to a string (the `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` SDK only stringifies single-text-block arrays). A session with a prior PDF `read` fails **permanently** on these gateways.

**vs. #42263** — that one is about the memory/OOM cost of re-sending base64 attachments each turn. Mine is a hard request rejection (422): the session is bricked, not just heavy. Same data flow, different symptom and different fix locus (message serialization vs. storage/compaction).

**vs. #39824** — that one is about media bypassing modality checks. Here the modality check **passed** (the model does declare PDF support), and that is precisely what sends the `file` block downstream to a gateway that doesn't implement it regardless of declared capabilities.

**Concrete, provider-agnostic fix unique to this report:**

1. In `message-v2.ts` (extraction logic, lines ~296-313 and ~380-399): treat `@ai-sdk/openai-compatible` as file-block-incapable — don't create the synthetic user message with `file` parts; append a textual marker to the tool output instead (pattern already used in `compaction.ts:73-78` and the `stripMedia` path).
2. In `transform.ts` (`unsupportedParts`, lines ~409-445), defense-in-depth: after filtering, collapse any user message whose content array is all-`text` blocks back into a plain `content: string` (joined with `\n\n`).

If the team prefers merging this into #41163 as a tracking issue, fine by me — just noting the 422-on-user-content-array failure mode isn't currently covered by the three referenced reports.

The bot is right that this overlaps #47885, and #47885 is the better report — it predates this by
five days and covers strictly more.

In particular it catches a half I missed: the same early return collapses `directory` to
`path.parse(input).root` as well as the id, so two unrelated non-git directories are
indistinguishable *and* `worktree === "/"` breaks path-relative permission scoping. That is a more
serious consequence than the attribution problem I described here, and it is not addressed by my
PR at all.

So treat this issue as a duplicate of #47885 for the root cause. What I would keep from it:

- **The measurement**, if it is useful as corroboration: 411 of 693 sessions on one machine in
  `global`, concentrated in a handful of parent directories each holding several checkouts. That is
  #47885's "workspace root above multiple repos" case, at scale, under automated dispatch.
- **#48871**, which is narrower than #47885's proposed direction and, I think, complementary rather
  than competing. #47885 argues identity should key on the normalized directory path, with git as an
  enrichment/merge signal. Under that scheme every directory becomes its own project, which fixes
  the collision — but it still gives no way to say *"this parent directory belongs to the project its
  checkouts belong to"*. My PR adds exactly that, via the `project_directory` table that already
  exists, as a fallback that never overrides git discovery.

Happy for a maintainer to close this in favour of #47885. If the directory-path-identity direction
lands first I would rebase #48871 onto it, since the association lookup sits in the same branch of
`resolve` either way.

Data point from the **v2 line** + a workaround validated in production on **v2.0.3** (originally reported in #48883, closed as duplicate of this issue / #33884).

**Reproduces on v2.0.3** with a package TUI plugin (`opencode plugin add`, install under `~/.cache/opencode/npm/...`): the widget paints its initial frame and then never repaints, even though the async fetcher resolves — verified with a non-reactive trace surfaced through a host dialog (fetch settles 200 in ~500 ms, resource resolves `ok=true`, UI frozen). Without local `solid-js`/`@opentui` copies in the install, the plugin instead fails to load entirely:

```
plugin operation failed ... stage=load
error="Cannot find package '@opentui/solid' imported from .../node_modules/<pkg>/src/tui.tsx"
```

**Additional detail on the resolution split** (reading `@opentui/core/runtime-plugin.js` against observed v2.0.3 behavior):

- Bare specifiers written in the plugin source (`import ... from "solid-js"`, `"@opencode/plugin/tui"`) **do** get rewritten to host runtime modules even inside `node_modules` — the prescan path (`nodeModulesRuntimeSpecifiers: true`) installs exact-path rewrite loaders for node_modules files whose source imports match the runtime map.
- The `@opentui/solid/jsx-runtime` / `jsx-dev-runtime` import **generated by the tsx transform** is emitted after the textual rewrite, so it is never rewritten. Bun then resolves it from the node_modules importer against the package's local copy (dual runtime), or fails when no copy exists.
- Net result: the plugin's signals/resources run on the **host's** `solid-js`, while the component tree runs on the package's **local** `@opentui/solid` — the initial frame renders, nothing ever repaints.

**Workaround — works today with no host changes.** Publish the plugin importing the host modules through their virtual ids, and avoid JSX syntax (explicit `jsx()`/`jsxs()` calls with per-expression getters — the same output shape the Solid JSX compiler emits, so no auto-generated bare JSX-runtime import exists):

```ts
import { createMemo, createResource, createSignal, onCleanup, Show } from "opentui:runtime-module:solid-js"
import { Plugin, usePlugin } from "opentui:runtime-module:%40opencode%2Fplugin%2Ftui"
import { jsx, jsxs } from "opentui:runtime-module:%40opentui%2Fsolid%2Fjsx-runtime"
```

Notes:

- Virtual `opentui:runtime-module:*` ids resolve through `build.module` registrations, which work regardless of the importer's location — the one path that reliably lands on host instances from inside `node_modules`.
- Import from `jsx-runtime`, not `jsx-dev-runtime`: the latter only re-exports `Fragment` and `jsxDEV`, the former exports `jsx` and `jsxs` as well.
- Declaring `solid-js`/`@opentui/*` peers as **optional** (`peerDependenciesMeta`) keeps npm from auto-installing shadow copies into plugin installs; with virtual imports the local copies are irrelevant anyway.

Live reference: [`@pistonex/opencode-go-usage`](https://github.com/pistonex/opencode-go-usage) on npm — **0.1.2** exhibits the frozen-UI failure, **0.1.3** carries the workaround. Installed as a package, data loads, hot language switching, 5-minute auto-refresh and collapse/expand all work.

For the eventual fix, the two candidate seams this analysis points at are: (a) letting the tsx transform emit the virtual runtime-module id for the JSX runtime import, or (b) enabling bare-specifier rewriting for plugin install directories — both would make the documented author shape (plain JSX + peerDependencies) work as published.

Data point: still reproduces on the **v2 line** (v2.0.3, packaged CLI) via the frozen-reactivity path — a package TUI plugin renders its initial frame and never repaints (dual reactive graph), or fails to load with `Cannot find package '@opentui/solid'` when the install has no local copies.

The v2.0.3 resolution details and a production-validated workaround (host virtual `opentui:runtime-module:*` imports, no JSX syntax — reference package `@pistonex/opencode-go-usage` on npm, 0.1.2 broken / 0.1.3 workaround) are posted on #39986.
